reasoning: As of March 6, 2026, Keir Starmer remains Prime Minister despite severe crises in February 2026. Evidence shows he survived the Peter Mandelson scandal and resignations of key aides (McSweeney, Allan) by securing cabinet backing and Parliamentary Labour Party support. While facing historic unpopularity (-50 approval), low polling (20%), and internal pressure, Starmer has repeatedly declared he will not resign and received standing ovations from MPs. Critical tests remain: May 7 local elections and February 26 by-election results. However, he has demonstrated resilience through the immediate crisis. The question asks if he ceases to be PM during 2026 (by Dec 31). Given his defiant stance, lack of clear successor, and survival of the February crisis, but considering ongoing instability, poor electoral prospects, and conditional cabinet support pending May elections, the probability of his departure remains elevated but not certain.
